text:
alyssa: Hey team, running into a customer escalations — they send a giant list (~120k short texts) to our embeddings endpoint and keep getting 413 Payload Too Large. They tried streaming/chunked uploads from their node client but still hit 413. Also saw a couple 400 errors earlier: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 4096". Need quick triage, possible customer impact (batching/throughput).

sam: Thanks — do we know which model they're hitting and whether they're compressing the payload? 413 usually means request body exceeds nginx/gateway limit (or our nginx limit per request), not per-customer token quota.

alyssa: They're using model `text-embedding-3-small` in the request body. Their client code was sending one huge JSON array of all inputs. No gzip.

kim: Ok couple of things: 1) dimension mismatch likely because some vectors saved from a different model variant got mixed in (e.g., outputs from `3-large` are 3072?). For our models: text-embedding-3-small = 1536, text-embedding-3-large = 3072 (double-check in model catalog). 2) 413 is gateway-level. Suggest short-term workaround: split into N-sized chunks (we usually recommend batch_size 2048 tokens or 2k items depending on item length) and gzip the payload.

ops-oncall: Poking infra — our front gateway limit currently 8MB for request body. If they send 120k items, they exceed that easily. We can either: a) advise chunking on client; b) support streaming POST with Transfer-Encoding: chunked upstream (we don't accept multipart streaming for embeddings yet); c) increase gateway limit for the tenant (risky).

alyssa: Customer also reported intermittent 401 earlier, then billing 402 when retried at higher rate. Could be auth token rotation + retries. Their user flow: upload list -> get 401 -> refresh token -> retry in bigger batch -> 413. So we need to communicate robust client pattern.

sam: Repro steps I used locally to emulate:
```bash
# generate 50k tiny records (simulate 120k)
python -c "import json; print(json.dumps([\"x\"*32]*50000))" > payload.json
# send raw (will 413 locally if >8MB)
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
  --data-binary @payload.json
```
This reproduces 413 for large files.

kim: Suggested client chunking snippet (python):
```python
def chunked_embed(client, inputs, chunk_size=2048):
    for i in range(0, len(inputs), chunk_size):
        chunk = inputs[i:i+chunk_size]
        yield client.embeddings.create(model=\"text-embedding-3-small\", input=chunk)
```
Notes: pick chunk_size so compressed payload < gateway limit (8MB). Use gzip: set `Content-Encoding: gzip` on requests and compress JSON bytes.

alyssa: Also told them to verify model and existing stored vectors. The dimension mismatch message they saw: `400 {\"error\":\"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 4096\"}`. That indicates some entries in their DB were produced by a different model or double-serialized. Quick check: sample a few existing vectors and compare length.

sam: Another tip: when looping over a large data set, do not accumulate JSON for the whole dataset in memory. Stream-generator or write temporary chunk files. Example node-ish pseudo:
```js
async function uploadInChunks(items, chunkSize=1000){
  for (let i=0;i<items.length;i+=chunkSize){
    const chunk = items.slice(i,i+chunkSize);
    await fetch('/v1/embeddings',{
      method:'POST',
      headers:{'Authorization':`Bearer ${TOKEN}`,'Content-Type':'application/json','Content-Encoding':'gzip'},
      body: gzip(JSON.stringify({model:'text-embedding-3-small', input:chunk}))
    });
  }
}
```

ops-oncall: FYI infra change ticket created if we want tenant-level increase: INC-2026-8421. But preferred path: client-side chunking + gzip + backoff. If customer insists, we can consider temporary increase and watch for abuse.

alyssa: Customer also worried about throughput — they want max throughput so trying to max batch size. We should give guidance: cost vs latency tradeoff. Large batch increases compute/window and memory, but you get better throughput. For embeddings, default is batching on our side; for huge arrays better to do parallel concurrent chunk requests (N workers) rather than single monolithic request.

kim: Also add note on idempotency: include client-side idempotency keys when re-issuing chunk uploads to avoid duplicate vector inserts.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-9142. Patch notes: recommended chunking, gzip, confirm model dims, retry with exponential backoff (jitter).

alyssa: Proposed reply to customer (draft):
- We recommend splitting input into chunks so each request stays under ~6MB compressed (we cap at ~8MB upstream; 6MB gives margin).
- Use gzip (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) to reduce payload size.
- Use chunk sizes of ~1k-2k items depending on avg text length.
- Parallelize by sending multiple chunk requests concurrently (4-8 workers) instead of 1 huge request.
- Confirm model `text-embedding-3-small` parameters and that any previously stored vectors came from same model (1536 dim). If you see "dimension mismatch" it's because some vectors are from a different model.
- If you still want us to accept huge monolithic uploads, we can explore a tenant gateway limit increase but need security and abuse review.

sam: I'll add a small client helper gist with chunking + gzip + retry and post link. Any objections to support-bot attaching the gist?

kim: No objections. Also add a fallback in their ingestion pipeline: detect server 413 -> automatically reduce chunk size and retry. 401 -> re-auth then retry once. 402/billing -> stop and surface to billing team.

alyssa: Customer asked about streaming chunked uploads using Transfer-Encoding: chunked — we currently don't support continuous streaming JSON arrays for embeddings. You must send discrete POST requests per chunk. We can document that.

ops-oncall: Leaving a note: consider docs update to recommend compression + chunking patterns for large embedding batches and include sample snippets. Filing DOCS-478.

alyssa: OK I'll reply to the customer with the draft + link to gist once Sam posts it. Marking this resolved from support side unless infra needs to bump limits. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: Gist posted: https://gist.github.com/redwood/embed-chunking-example (will attach to ticket).
